protocol.negative_sampling: same time step as the real edge, no existing edge
protocol.link_evaluation_graph: validation: train edges; test: train + validation edges
protocol.feature_scaling: mean/std from labelled training nodes only, fitted per split protocol

evidence_table.Finding: The constraint lowers link scores for illicit-licit pairs
evidence_table.Reason (offered): The penalty is applied to exactly these pairs during training.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): Constraint reduction on held-out test edges (temporal): 1A -0.015, 1B 0.237. Difference +0.252 (95% CI +0.225 to +0.278), 1B higher in 8/8 seeds.

evidence_table.Finding: Effect of the constraint on illicit-class F1 and average precision on the main temporal split (steps 35-49)
evidence_table.Reason (offered): Row 1 shows the constraint acts on link scores, row 3 that it separates the classes. Whether separation is the cause is tested in row 4.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): F1 @0.5 +0.100 (95% CI +0.068 to +0.132), higher in 8/8 seeds. F1 @validated +0.074 (95% CI +0.044 to +0.105), higher in 8/8 seeds. Average precision +0.118 (95% CI +0.086 to +0.149), higher in 8/8 seeds. Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon p: F1 @validated 0.0234, AP 0.0234.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Paired seed-level evidence on one fixed split. In the further windows and folds tested, the F1 gain is clearly positive in 2 of 4 and the AP gain in 2 of 2 folds (rows 11 and 12).

evidence_table.Finding: The constraint increases class separation in the shared embedding
evidence_table.Reason (offered): The penalty makes illicit-licit pairs score low on a dot-product decoder, which pulls their embeddings apart.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): Silhouette of illicit vs licit nodes (temporal): training nodes 1A 0.162, 1B 0.304 (difference +0.142, 1B higher in 8/8). Test nodes 1A -0.067, 1B -0.003 (difference +0.065, 1B higher in 8/8). Separation ratio, test nodes: +0.060.

evidence_table.Finding: Whether added class separation produces the F1 gain
evidence_table.Reason (offered): Hypothesis: the node head reads the same embedding, so more separation should mean better classification.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): Per-seed Spearman correlation between added test-node separation and added F1 (temporal): rho +0.12, p 0.779, n = 8. Over all 40 lambda-by-seed runs: separation against F1 rho +0.23 (p 0.146), and within a fixed lambda rho -0.17 (p 0.305). Random split: separation difference +0.129, F1 @0.5 difference -0.021.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Not supported by these data: across the eight seeds the added separation does not track the added F1 (rho +0.12, p 0.78); on the random split test-node separation rises (+0.129) while F1 at 0.5 does not (-0.021); within a fixed lambda, seeds with more separation do not score higher (rho -0.17, p 0.31). Separation rises with the constraint, but these data do not show it is the cause of the F1 gain.

evidence_table.Reason (offered): If the constraint causes the gain, performance should change with its weight.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Direct measurement. Link AUC falls monotonically with lambda: True. Reduction rises monotonically: True. F1 is highest at lambda 1.

evidence_table.Finding: Effect of the constraint under a random split
evidence_table.Reason (offered): Hypothesis: when training and test data match there is little to gain, and the penalty also lowers scores for real illicit-licit edges.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): F1 @0.5: -0.021 (95% CI -0.033 to -0.008), higher in 1/8 seeds. F1 @validated: +0.004 (95% CI -0.006 to +0.014), higher in 4/8 seeds. Average precision: +0.006 (95% CI +0.002 to +0.010), higher in 7/8 seeds. 1A test-node silhouette: temporal -0.067, random 0.056.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Measured. At the default threshold F1 is lower, at the validated threshold not different, and average precision is higher. The explanation is a hypothesis.

evidence_table.Reason (offered): Real transactions also link illicit and licit nodes, and the penalty teaches the model to score them low.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): Link AUC temporal -0.084 (95% CI -0.097 to -0.071), higher in 0/8 seeds. Random -0.052 (95% CI -0.057 to -0.046), higher in 0/8 seeds. Mean score of real illicit-licit edges (temporal): 1A 0.751, 1B 0.493.

evidence_table.Finding: A random split overstates performance because the periods differ
evidence_table.Reason (offered): Features reveal when a transaction happened, and the class balance shifts, so a model tested on the future meets a distribution it was not trained on.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): Domain classifier AUC: training vs test period 1.000, random control 0.499. Illicit share: 0.109 (train period), 0.065 (test period). 1A F1 @0.5: random 0.836, temporal 0.440.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Direct measurement. An AUC this close to 1 means the features identify the period almost perfectly, which is consistent with the look-ahead in Elliptic features reported by Safar et al. (2026). This notebook does not test that explanation.

evidence_table.Finding: No future information can reach training through message passing
evidence_table.Reason (offered): Every edge joins two nodes in the same time step, so adding test-period edges cannot change the neighbourhood of a training node.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): 100.0000% of edges lie inside one time step. Strict and transductive temporal training give identical results in the multi-seed ablation, and agree to about 1e-14 in double precision (archive notebook).

evidence_table.Finding: Random forest compared with the graph models, by window
evidence_table.Reason (offered): The graph models are small and untuned, and Elliptic carries much of its signal in aggregated features that a tree model uses directly.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): Whole test period F1 @validated: random forest 0.801, 1B 0.608. AP 0.786 against 0.648. Steps 35-42: random forest 0.896, 1B 0.696, 1A 0.645, node-only 0.604. Steps 43-49: random forest 0.028, 1B 0.023, 1A 0.035, node-only 0.018. Published Weber et al. random forest: 0.788.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Direct measurement. The explanation is a hypothesis. After step 43 no model is better than the others (row 11).

evidence_table.Reason (offered): A regime change: the illicit behaviour in this period differs from anything in the training window.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): F1 @validated, steps 43-49: Node-only 0.018, 1A 0.035, 1B 0.023, Random forest 0.028. Steps 35-42: Node-only 0.604, 1A 0.645, 1B 0.696, Random forest 0.896.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Direct measurement. The cause (a dark-market shutdown at step 43 is reported in the Elliptic literature) is not tested here.

evidence_table.Finding: Stability of the temporal gain across windows and folds
evidence_table.Reason (offered): The same comparison is repeated on other test windows and on earlier training and test periods.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Replication is partial: the F1 gain is clearly positive in 2 of 4 further windows or folds, and the AP gain in 2 of 2 folds.

evidence_table.Finding: Whether validation data can choose lambda
evidence_table.Reason (offered): The validation window is short, so validation F1 is noisy.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): Mean best validation F1 by lambda: 0.1 0.810, 0.5 0.832, 1 0.820, 2 0.834. Largest SD across seeds: 0.027.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Range of validation F1 across lambda 0.024, against a largest SD of 0.027. Differences are within one SD, so lambda = 1 stays an a priori choice.

evidence_table.Finding: Combined and interacting effects of the five pipeline flaws
evidence_table.Reason (offered): Labels from non-training nodes, easy link negatives, held-out edges in the link graph, a scaler fitted on all nodes and premature early stopping each give the model information or a shortcut it should not have.
evidence_table.Proof (numbers): Gain of 1B over 1A (F1 @validated): final pipeline +0.074, all five together +0.164. Each variant: 1. constraint sees all node labels: +0.074; 2. negatives from any time step: +0.010; 3. held-out edges in the link graph: +0.088; 4. scaler fitted on all nodes: +0.037; 5. no early-stopping warm-up: +0.099; flaws 1+2: leaked labels with any-step negatives: +0.156; all five except flaw 1 (labels not leaked): -0.017. 1A link AUC: final 0.697, with held-out edges in the link graph 0.830.
evidence_table.Strength of evidence: Controlled re-introduction of each flaw. The effects are not additive: some single flaws leave the gain unchanged or reduce it, so attribute the inflation to the combination.

mechanism_control.verdict_1S: 1S is worse than 1A: a penalty on meaningless labels hurts, so the 1B gain is not a generic regularisation effect.

verdict_1E.1E w=1 (embedding, no link penalty): 1E w=1 (embedding, no link penalty): reaches the separation of 1B on training nodes (silhouette 0.43 against 0.30) and shows no gain, so separation alone is not sufficient to produce the 1B gain.
verdict_1E.1E w=5 (embedding, no link penalty): 1E w=5 (embedding, no link penalty): reaches the separation of 1B on training nodes (silhouette 0.42 against 0.30) and shows no gain, so separation alone is not sufficient to produce the 1B gain.
